text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Out of 3,353,090 counted ballots votes, 1,601,438 went to the coalition of the Socialist Party of Serbia , United Yugoslav Left and New Democracy, said the Socialist Party spokesman Ivica Dacic.
- Yugoslavia's internal debt of about 10 billion German marks burdens the country's economy and limits its further development, said the Institute of Econimic Sciences.
- Leader of the Yugoslav United Left (JUL) Mirjana Markovic, said JUL intends to strenghten its net in Serbia and establish and organise it in Montenegro.
- The Serbian Radical party says it is extremely satisfied with election results which according to preliminary figures show it won 30 percent more votes compared to previous 1993 elections.
- The Montenegrin ruling Democratic Party of Socialists secured 45 seats or 60 percent in republic's parliament.
- The Ministry for Agriculture said wheat sown on 600,000 hectares by October 28, or half the planned acerage.

- Industrial production this year could grow about seven percent compared to 1995 but at the cost of a high trade deficit which is expected to surge to $1.8-1.9 billion, the Belgrade-based Institute for Economic Sciences said. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
